Obloquy
ŏb´lō-kwy
n. (censorious speech; reproach cast on a name; the state of being spoken against)
Latin obloquium, from ob-, against, and loqui, to speak — a speaking against. It is the ordinary weather of the Christian's public life, and the New Testament treats it as such.

Biblical Definition

Obloquy is being spoken against. The Jews at Rome say of the Christian faith, “as concerning this sect, we know that every where it is spoken against” (Act 28:22). Paul reports it as his ordinary condition: “being defamed, we intreat: we are made as the filth of the world, and are the offscouring of all things unto this day” (1Co 4:13). David knows it: “I have heard the slander of many: fear was on every side” (Psa 31:13). The Lord makes it a beatitude when it is false and for His sake (Mat 5:11). And Peter turns it into evidence: “If ye be reproached for the name of Christ, happy are ye; for the spirit of glory and of God resteth upon you” (1Pe 4:14).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines obloquy as censorious speech; reproachful language; language that casts contempt on men or their actions; and cause of reproach; disgrace.

OBLOQUY, n. Censorious speech; reproachful language; language that casts contempt on men or their actions.

Shall names that made your city the glory of the earth, be censured and defamed in the obloquy of a few?

2. Cause of reproach; disgrace.

Key Scripture

Act 28:22 — "But we desire to hear of thee what thou thinkest: for as concerning this sect, we know that every where it is spoken against."

1Co 4:13 — "Being defamed, we intreat: we are made as the filth of the world, and are the offscouring of all things unto this day."

Psa 31:13 — "For I have heard the slander of many: fear was on every side: while they took counsel together against me, they devised to take away my life."

Mat 5:11 — "Blessed are ye, when men shall revile you, and persecute you, and shall say all manner of evil against you falsely, for my sake."

1Pe 4:14 — "If ye be reproached for the name of Christ, happy are ye; for the spirit of glory and of God resteth upon you: on their part he is evil spoken of, but on your part he is glorified."

Modern Corruption

Being spoken against is taken as proof of faithfulness, and Peter attaches conditions to the comfort.

expand to see more

The comfort is real and it is conditional, and both halves must be kept. First Peter 4:14 promises the spirit of glory to those reproached for the name of Christ, and the very next verse removes the loophole: but let none of you suffer as a murderer, or as a thief, or as an evildoer, or as a busybody in other men's matters. The last item is the pointed one. A Christian may attract genuine hostility by interfering, by rudeness, by a manner that has nothing of Christ in it, and then claim the beatitude — and Peter names that exact case and excludes it.

The opposite error is to treat all obloquy as a signal that something has gone wrong. Acts 28:22 records the faith being everywhere spoken against at the outset, before any Christian had done anything to deserve it, and 1 Corinthians 4:13 has an apostle describing himself as the offscouring of all things. A church whose reputation is uniformly good among people who reject its Lord should ask what it has stopped saying. The gospel names sin, claims exclusivity and calls for repentance, and there is no arrangement of tone that makes those universally welcome.

Between the two errors lies the discipline of not answering. Paul's phrase in 1 Corinthians 4:13 is being defamed, we intreat — and the pattern beneath it is 1 Peter 2:23, who when He was reviled, reviled not again, but committed Himself to Him that judgeth righteously. That is not passivity; it is a transfer of the case to a court with better evidence. A man's name is one of the things he may hand over, and the last verdict on it will not be delivered by the people currently discussing him.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Greek antilego (G483), to speak against; dusphemeo (G1425), to defame; oneidizo (G3679), to reproach; perikatharma / peripsema (G4027, G4067), filth, offscouring.

expand to see more

Greek antilegetai (G483) — it is spoken against; Acts 28:22, Luke 2:34, Titus 1:9, 2:9.

Greek dusphemoumenoi (G1425) — being defamed; 1 Corinthians 4:13 only.

Greek oneidizo (G3679) — to reproach; 1 Peter 4:14, Matthew 5:11, Romans 15:3.

Usage

"“Every where it is spoken against” — said of the faith at the outset."

"“Being defamed, we intreat” — and the case is transferred, not argued."

"“Let none of you suffer… as a busybody” — the loophole Peter closes."
